uncited: This family explores alternative mechanisms for computing skinning weights and deformations in Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) for Gaussian Splatting, specifically comparing learned networks against deterministic template-based approaches.

It addresses the limitations of fixed skinning weights by investigating whether conditioning on pose or using learned mappings improves reconstruction quality and reduces artifacts in animatable human avatars.

All variants in this family operate within the framework of Linear Blend Skinning for Gaussian Splatting, where canonical 3D Gaussians are deformed using precomputed rigid joint transformations and learnable or deterministic skinning weights.
The core objective is to map points from the canonical space to the posed space while maintaining geometric consistency and visual fidelity.
A key distinction in the implementation of these variants involves the handling of global transformations.
This ensures that the local pose conditioning is applied relative to a consistent global frame.
The performance of these variants is evaluated using Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) on standard datasets.
Backward LBS conditions the skinning weight network on the local body poses $\theta$.
This variant uses nearest neighbor SMPL skinning weights derived from the template mesh.
The study highlights the trade-offs between learned flexibility and deterministic stability in skinning weight computation.
